summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for a flare characterized by total body pain, shortness of breath, pruritus, and hand swelling, which she attributed to being off Enbrel for two weeks. She was treated with IV diphenhydramine, Dilaudid, and lorazepam, with symptom improvement. A chest CT revealed pulmonary nodules suspicious for infection or inflammation, prompting a CT-guided lung biopsy. Biopsy results showed no organisms or growth, and no immediate complications occurred. She was transitioned to oral medications, discharged home, and scheduled for follow-up with pulmonology and rheumatology. Her Enbrel was held pending further evaluation of the lung findings.
